info.title: About Network Simulator
info.adminOnly: Administrators can check for and install updates here.

updates.title: Updates
updates.subtitle: Check for new versions, install them and switch between the production and test channel.
updates.confirmText: The server makes a database backup, builds the new version, migrates the database and restarts. This takes a few minutes; everyone stays signed in. If the new version does not start, the previous version is put back automatically.
updates.downgradeWarning: Going back from test to production can mean an older version. Database changes from the test version are not undone; if production does not start, the backup made before the switch is restored.
updates.howItWorks: Updates come from the GitHub repository: the production channel follows the production branch, the test channel the test branch. The helper service network-simulator-update installs them with root rights; the web interface itself never does.

dashboard.intro: Design networks, configure virtual Cisco-style routers and switches from the CLI, and watch packets travel to see at a glance what works.
dashboard.roadmapText: The platform is built in four phases.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.subtitle: Your own SMTP server for notifications such as failed backups.
mail.enabledHint: Turn off to stop all outgoing mail.

securityHint.starttls: Usually port 587. The connection must be upgraded to TLS, otherwise nothing is sent.
securityHint.tls: Usually port 465. Encrypted from the first byte.
securityHint.none: Only for a relay on the local network.

mail.verifyCertHint: Turn off only for a server with a self-signed certificate.
mail.insecure: Without encryption the password and the messages travel in plain text.
mail.dkimHint: Sign messages with your own DKIM key so they pass SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks. Publish the public key as selector._domainkey.domain.
mail.testHint: Sends a test message with the settings in the form, also before you save them.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.subtitle: Encrypted full and incremental backups to FTP, FTPS or SCP, and restore from any of them.
backup.name: Name
backup.privateKeyHint: OpenSSH or PEM format. Add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the backup user.
backup.pathHint: Relative to the home folder of the user, or an absolute path.
backup.implicitTlsHint: Port 990. Off means explicit TLS (AUTH TLS) on port 21.
backup.verifyCertHint: Off for a self-signed certificate: you then trust its fingerprint after the test.
backup.ftpWarning: Plain FTP sends the password unencrypted. The backup itself is always encrypted. Use SCP or FTPS when you can.
backup.enabledHint: Off pauses scheduled backups to this location; restoring still works.
backup.testOk: Connection works: a test file was written, read and deleted.
backup.testOkExisting: Connection works. Existing Network Simulator backups were found in this folder.
backup.fingerprintUnknown: First connection: compare this fingerprint with the server and trust it.
backup.fingerprintChanged: The fingerprint of the server has changed! Only trust it if you know why (for example a new server).
backup.trusted: Fingerprint trusted. Test again to check the connection.
backup.noLocationsText: Add a NAS, server or hosting account to store encrypted backups.
backup.confirmDelete: Delete location {{name}}? The backups at the location itself stay.
backup.started: Backup to {{name}} started. Follow it under History.
backup.scheduleHint: Runs to every enabled location. Missed backups run when the server is back.
backup.keepHint: Older ones are deleted with their incrementals.
backup.retentionSummary: You can go back about {{weeks}} week(s).
backup.needPassphrase: Set a backup passphrase first: without it no backup runs.
backup.encryptionText: Every backup is compressed and encrypted (AES-256-GCM) before it leaves the server. The key is protected by your passphrase.
backup.storePassphrase: Store the passphrase in your password manager. Without it nobody can restore the backups, including you.
backup.passUnreachable: Passphrase saved, but these locations could not be updated: {{names}}. Their existing backups still use the old passphrase.
backup.otherHint: Restore from a location that is not set up on this server, for example after installing a new server.
backup.passphraseOptional: Leave empty to use the passphrase set on this server.
backup.passphraseOther: The passphrase of the server that made the backups.
backup.confirmRestoreText: All current data is replaced by the backup of {{date}}. The server restarts and everyone is signed out. The current state is kept until the next restore and is put back automatically if the restore fails.
backup.restoreSignIn: Sign in again with an account from the backup.

restoreState.staged: Verified. The server restarts to apply it…
restoreState.rolled-back: Restore failed: the previous state was put back
